chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon them), who said:
We order our children to perform Salat when they are five years old, so you should order your children to perform Salat when they are seven years old.

And we order our children to fast when they are seven years old, with whatever they can bear from fasting the day, whether it is up to half the day, or more than that, or less. So when thirst and hunger overcome them, they break their fast, until they become accustomed to fasting and are able to endure it.
So order your children to fast when they are nine years old, for whatever they can bear of fasting the day. So when thirst overcomes them, they break their fast.
ai.seo_question: At what age should children start praying and fasting according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the pedagogical framework for *Tadrib* (training) rather than immediate obligation, reflecting the Shia scholarly consensus that pre-pubertal children are not yet bound by *Taklif*. It highlights a gradualist approach where prayer instruction begins at age five to build habit, while fasting is introduced at age seven with flexibility for physical limits, culminating in full-day fasting expectations by age nine.
